rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani derives the devil’s agitation from a root meaning cutting, hence cutting people off from right guidance.
rows.anchor: أي استزله بقطعه عن الصواب - قاله الرماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to agitate means to make people frivolous and lure them away from what is right.
rows.anchor: أي استخف , والفز أصله القطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil’s voice includes invitations to wealth, music, and every whisper by which he adorns sin.
rows.anchor: أي دعائك بالغنى والمزامير وكل ما تزينه بالوساس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil is told to summon all the forces he can, while his power remains limited to what God permits.
rows.anchor: المعنى : افعل جميع ما تقدر عليه , ولا تدع شيئا من قوتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil shares in people’s affairs by joining them when they act in ways that satisfy his desires.
rows.anchor: أي بوثوبك على مخالطتهم عند ما يشاركونك بفعل ما يوافق هواك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharing in wealth and children includes unlawful earnings, omitting God’s name, pagan sacrifices, forbidden spending, and teaching children sin or unbelief.
rows.anchor: إن اقتنوها بوجه محرم أو لم يذكروا اسمي عليها , وكذا قرابينهم لغير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil promises false hopes such as idols’ intercession, honor with God, and postponing repentance.
rows.anchor: من المواعيد الباطلة ما يستخفهم ويغرهم من شفاعة الآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Delusion is dressing error in a way that makes it seem correct.
rows.anchor: والغرور : تزيين الخطأ بما يوهم أنه صواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s chosen servants fulfill servitude through piety and excellence; the devil has no authority to lead them into unforgiven sin.
rows.anchor: الذين أهلتهم للإضافة إلي فقاموا بحق عبودتي بالتقوى والإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God protects these servants by granting them reliance on Him, and is sufficient as their guardian.
rows.anchor: فإني وفقتهم للتوكل علي فكفيتهم أمرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea passage returns to proofs of divine oneness and calls the hearers toward repentance through God’s care for them.
rows.anchor: عودا إلى دلائل التوحيد الذي هو المقصود الأعظم بأحوال البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God propels ships through the sea for people’s benefit, making available benefits difficult to reach by land; Noah also carried their ancestor in a ship.
rows.anchor: { الذي يزجي } أي يسوق ويدفع وينفذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy is addressed especially to believers.
rows.anchor: { بكم } أي أيها المؤمنون خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may also encompass all humanity, whom God distinguished from animals through this provision.
rows.anchor: أو يكون ذلك خطابا لجميع النوع فيكون المعنى : خصكم به من بين الحيوانات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording attributes good to God rather than directly assigning evil to Him, as a matter of proper speech though all things are His act.
rows.anchor: تأديبا لنا في مخاطبته بنسبة الخير دون الشر إليه , مع اعتقاده أن الكل فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In danger at sea, every invoked being vanishes from memory except God, since people know only He can save them.
rows.anchor: أي ذهب وبطل عن ذكركم وخواطركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once brought safely to land, people abandon exclusive devotion and return to associating partners with God; ingratitude marks humanity generally, save those God purifies.
rows.anchor: عن الإخلاص له ورجعتم إلى الإشراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should fear God equally on every side of land, since His power to bury them in earth is equal to His power at sea.
rows.anchor: قدرتنا على التغييب في التراب في جميع الجوانب كقدرتنا على التغييب في الماء سواء

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi explains a hailstorm as something that pelts people with small stones.
rows.anchor: أي يرمي بالحصباء , أي بالحصى الصغار - قاله الرازي في اللوامع

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani glosses the hailstorm as stones thrown repeatedly at people.
rows.anchor: وقال الرماني : حجارة يحصب بها , أي يرمي بها , حصبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the hailstorm to be a wind; the masculine form is used because the adjective is not transferred to a feminine noun.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الحاصب : الريح , ولم يقل : حاصبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hailstorm recalls the punishment sent against Lot’s people.
rows.anchor: كما وقع لقوم لوط أنا أرسلنا عليهم حاصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As at sea, no guardian can rescue people from danger on land.
rows.anchor: ينجيكم من ذلك ولا من غيره كما لم تجدوا في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may return people to the sea by compelling causes, then send a violently breaking wind and drown them for unbelief.
rows.anchor: قاصفا } وهو الكاسر بشدة { من الريح } كما عهدتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares drowning for unbelief to a person retaliating against someone who denies his kindness.
rows.anchor: { بما كفرتم } كما يفعل أحدكم إذا ظفر بمن كفر إحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can demand recompense from God; placing “against Us” first signals majesty.
rows.anchor: وقدم قوله تعالى : { علينا } دلالة على باهر العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing word tabeʿ means a claimant demanding that God answer for what He did.
rows.anchor: تبيعا * } أي مطالبا يطالبنا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity’s honor after the preceding signs demonstrates God’s ability to resurrect by differentiating beings that began alike.
rows.anchor: ليستدلوا بذلك على سهولة الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human soul is noblest among this world’s souls because it encompasses vegetative, sensory, voluntary-motion, and rational faculties and can know God and created realms.
rows.anchor: ركب جوهر الإنسان من نفس هي أشرف النفوس بما فضلها على قوى النفس النباتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human body is also distinguished by its upright stature and ability to reach and handle things with the hand.
rows.anchor: اعتدال القامة وامتدادها والتناول باليد وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of “honored” makes the honor general: humans surpass clay through growth, living things through life, and living creatures through speech.
rows.anchor: حذف متعلق التكريم دالا على عمومه لجميع الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God carries people over land on animals and over sea on ships.
rows.anchor: في البر } على الدواب وغيرها { والبحر } على السفن وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives people pleasant fruits and foods, while animals eat only the coarse remnants.
rows.anchor: أي المستلذات من الثمرات والأقوات التي يأكل غيرهم من الحيوان قشها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are favored in their form, knowledge that leads to felicity, and provision, yet the verse says “many” rather than all created beings.
rows.anchor: في أنفسهم بإحسان الشكل , وفي صفاتهم بالعلم المنتج لسعادة الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elect who discipline their flawed desires and attain piety and excellence are the best of creatures; the command that angels prostrate to Adam anticipates this rank.
rows.anchor: وأما الخلص فهم أفضل الخلائق لما علمنا من معالجتهم بالإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their imam” can mean the prophet each nation followed, after which authentic and false followers are distinguished.
rows.anchor: أي بمتبوعهم الذي كانوا يتبعونه , فيقال : يا أتباع نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, each people may be summoned by the deeds they pursued, bound to them like a follower to an imam; the author compares this with each person’s deed fastened to his neck.
rows.anchor: أو يكون المراد بسبب أعمالهم التي ربطناهم بها ربط المأموم بإمامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record books are handed to people after the recording angels have kept account of their deeds.
rows.anchor: وندفع إليهم الكتب التي أحصت حفظتنا فيها تلك الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given their record in the right hand are clear-hearted through piety and excellence, and already perceptive in worldly life.
rows.anchor: فهم البصراء القلوب لتقواهم وإحسانهم , وهم البصراء في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reread their records repeatedly out of joy, like anyone pleased by a book.
rows.anchor: يجددون قراءته ويكررونها سرورا بما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lose no good deed, and receive further reward according to sincerity, moral purity, and good works.
rows.anchor: يزادون بحسب إخلاص النيات وطهارة الأخلاق وزكاء الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person blind to what benefits or harms him in worldly conduct will be still blinder and farther from the way in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لا يهتدي إلى أخذ ما ينفعه وترك ما يضره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual blindness grows moment by moment, unlike fixed physical traits, so the verse does not say “more blind” in that ordinary sense.
rows.anchor: لم يقل : أشد عمى , كما يقولونه في الخلق اللازمة لحالة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr does not apply imāla to the second occurrence of “blind,” although he applies it to the first, to signal its comparative meaning.
rows.anchor: ولم يمله أبو عمرو مع إمالة الأول ليدل على أن معناه : أفعل من كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses use ellipsis by interlocking: right-hand delivery and reading imply their opposites are omitted, while the later blindness implies the opposite was omitted earlier.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : أثبت الإيتاء باليمين والقراءة أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents nearly seduce the Prophet from revelation despite its clarity and his discernment of deceit, because they are themselves blind to God’s protection.
rows.anchor: جبلت عليه من الفطنة , وجودة الفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “they nearly” distinguishes the softened emphatic إن from a negation.
rows.anchor: كانت ( إن ) مخففة من الثقيلة أتى باللام الفارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temptation sought to induce the Prophet to replace revelation with another message, perhaps by promising converts among people likely to accept Islam.
rows.anchor: إطماعا منهم في إسلام من هو بحيث يرجى إسلامه إسلام الجم الغفير

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani defines the root sense of temptation as seeking to extract something from what envelops it.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : وأصل الفتنة ما يطلب به خلاص الشيء مما لابسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “invent” carries the sense of deliberately cutting out or producing something else against God.
rows.anchor: أي تقطع متعمدا { علينا } على عظمتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had the Prophet inclined to them, they would have taken him as a close friend; friendship with unbelievers is incompatible with friendship with God.
rows.anchor: ومن كان خليل الكفار لم يكن خليل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet saw the right course and held to God’s command, so the opponents remained in their blindness.
rows.anchor: ولكنك أبصرت رشدك فلزمت أمر الله

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz distinguishes cutting leather for repair from cutting it for damage, with the hamza marking removal or corruption.
rows.anchor: وقال القزاز : الفري مصدر فريت الأديم - إذا شققته للإصلاح , وأفريته - إذا شققته للإفساد - كأن همزته للإزالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root farā means cutting; using it for lying means inventing a falsehood that exceeds truthful speech and its proper limit.
rows.anchor: فريت الشيء وأفريته : قطعته , وفرى الكذب وافتراه : اختلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making a waterskin expands its capacity; Al-Qazzaz says the term can mean sewing it because sewing occurs along the cut.
rows.anchor: وفرى المزادة : خلقها وصنعها , وقال القزاز : خرزها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also extends figuratively to traversing land, being bewildered by an excess of sensation, repairing, reproaching, or producing extraordinary work.
rows.anchor: وفرى الأرض : سارها وقطعها - تشبيها لها بالأديم , وفرى - كرضي : تحير ودهش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicons conflict over whether rifa means bran and tifa a predatory fox-like animal; the author prefers Mukhtaṣar al-ʿAyn’s account because Ibn al-Tibbani attributes it to the Kitāb al-ʿAyn.
rows.anchor: فاضظرب كلامه فوجب قبول مختصر العين

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa agrees that the tifa is a fox-like animal that hunts everything and eats only meat.
rows.anchor: لا تأكل إلا اللحم - أبو حنيفة مثله , كله انتهى بحروفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proverb about the tifa becoming independent of bran is quoted as an example of the disputed word usage.
rows.anchor: ويقال في مثل من الأمثال : استغنت التفه عن الرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicons differ on whether the pure-milk term al-arafī is formed from a yāʾ-root or a wāw-root.
rows.anchor: جعله المختصر يائيا , والقاموس واويا , ثم أعاده في المهموز

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz says rāfaytu means agreeing with someone, a broadening of social relations.
rows.anchor: رافيت الرجل أرافيه مرافاة - إذا وافقته - لأن ذلك أوسع في العشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root rīf names fertile, cultivated land and spaciousness in food and drink; arāfat al-arḍ means that the land became fertile.
rows.anchor: والريف بالكسر - الخصب , وقال في القاموس : أرض فيها زرع وخصب , والسعة في المأكل والمشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafāʾ can mean mooring a ship near shore, reconciling people, or drawing close, with the glosses explained through approach or expanded access.
rows.anchor: رفأ السفينة - كمنع وأرفأهاك أدناها من الشط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word yarfīʾ covers agile animals and a shepherd; the author connects this range to expansive movement and excess.
rows.anchor: واليرفيء كاليلمعي : راعي الغنم والظليم النافر والظبي القفوز المولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾf can refer to wine or a merciful person, and raʾfa is glossed as either the strongest or the most delicate mercy.
rows.anchor: والرأف : الخمر والرجل الرحيم , أو الرأفة : أشد الرحمة أو أرقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other related forms refer to a wild donkey, an island, a mouse, and a pot boiling fiercely; the author explains them through motion, abundance, or overflow.
rows.anchor: والفرأ - كجبل وسحاب : حمار الوحش أو الفتي منه - لشدة نفاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicon’s final derivatives include a noisy group, calamity, intense hardship, the onset of summer, and boundaries that restrict a space.
rows.anchor: الجماعة - وقيدها في مختصر العين بذات الجلبة - والبلية والاختلاط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s strengthening preserved the Prophet from any inclination, though he desired the opponents’ guidance and benefit.
rows.anchor: وكنا عصمناك فلم تركن إليهم لا قليلا ولا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lولا construction makes the prevented nearness to inclination depend on the actual divine strengthening; that strengthening exists and the inclination is absent.
rows.anchor: لانتفاء الثاني لأجل انتفاء الأول , وهي هنا داخلة على لا النافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading takes the implicit subject of “nearly” to be the opponents: their extreme deceit almost made the Prophet incline, as in saying someone nearly killed himself by his actions.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد الدلالة على شدة مكرهم وتناهي خداعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse proves the Prophet’s exceptional natural intelligence and virtue: even without the added protection of prophethood, he would not have inclined to such cunning opponents.
rows.anchor: لو وكل إلى نفسه وما خلق الله في طبعه وجبلته من الغرائز الكاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If he had inclined to them, God would have made him taste multiplied punishment in both worldly life and death.
rows.anchor: أي بعظمتنا { ضعف } عذاب { الحياة وضعف } عذاب { الممات } أي ذلك العذاب مضاعفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ḍaʿf is associated with weakness and its counterpart, strength; lexicographers also distinguish the vowelled forms as weakness of judgment versus body.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضعف بالفتح في العقل والرأي , وبالضم في الجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some lexicographers gloss ḍaʿīf as “blind” in Ḥimyarī, and call a weakly rained-on land muḍʿafa.
rows.anchor: والضعيف : الأعمى - حميرية , وأرض مضعفة للمفعول : أصابها مطر ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍaʿf can mean a counterpart or multiple; its basic sense is open-ended increase, and doubling may add two units to make three.
rows.anchor: وضاعفت الشيء , أي ضممت إلى الشيء شيئين فصار ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is a frail life and death multiplied many times; even the greatest person would find no helper against God.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى - والله أعلم : أذقناك وهي الحياة ووهي الممات مضاعفا أضعافا كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wrong is graver in proportion to the status of its perpetrator, and even slight accommodation to corrupt people opposes God and leaves His protection.
rows.anchor: القبيح يعظم قبحه بمقدار عظيم شأن مرتكبه وارتفاع منزلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents nearly drove the Prophet from Mecca through sustained harassment, despite his presence among them being a mercy.
rows.anchor: حتى كادوا أن يخرجوه من وطنه قبل الإذن الخاص بالهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they had expelled him, they would remain only briefly afterward; God fulfilled this threat with their leaders’ deaths at Badr eighteen months after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: بقتل صناديدهم في غزوة بدر في رمضان من السنة الثانية من الهجرة بعد ثمانية عشر شهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also barred the Meccan expellers from entering or settling in the sanctuary and Arabian Peninsula, honoring the Prophet and avenging their intent to annul his mission.
rows.anchor: وحرم على المشركين الذين أخرجوه صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم من مكة المشرفة الدخول إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plot of an ignorant person against a learned person returns as harm to the plotter in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: الجاهل لا يزال ينصب للعالم الحبائل , ويطلب له الغوائلن فيعود ذلك عليه بالوبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s established way is to punish those who accept the expulsion of a messenger after letting him live among them as a mercy.
rows.anchor: بين ظهراني قومهم رحمة لقومهم , فإذا أخرجوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan opponents are specially spared annihilation as a distinction granted through this Prophet, while God’s established way cannot be changed by another.
rows.anchor: لكنهم خصوا عن الأمم السالفة بأنهم لا يعذبون عذاب الاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A way of those sent before you” can be parsed as their way being applied to you, or as God’s way being the precedent for them.
rows.anchor: أي كسنة أو سنتنا بك سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer should be fully established with all its conditions, pillars, preliminaries, and ends; it is the core of worship and intimate communion with God.
rows.anchor: بفعل جميع شرائطها وأركانها ومبادئها وغاياتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is a great aid against enemies and hardship and a cause of well-being; the Prophet turned to prayer when distressed.
rows.anchor: أن الصلاة أعظم ناصر على الأعداء الذين يريدون بمكرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duluk is glossed as setting, yellowing, declining, or passing the meridian; using the term across its senses covers noon, afternoon, and sunset prayers.
rows.anchor: قال في القاموس : دلكت الشمس : غربت أو اصفرت أو مالت أو زالت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term also indicates that sunset prayer lasts until the twilight disappears; waiting for each time already counts as being in prayer.
rows.anchor: لأن الإنسان في صلاة ما كان ينتظر الصلاة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi defines ghassaq as the night’s darkness becoming fully established.
rows.anchor: وقال الرازي في اللوامع : وهو استحكام ظلمة الليل

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani instead glosses ghassaq as the appearance of night’s darkness.
rows.anchor: وقال الرماني : ظهور ظلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Qur’an of dawn” refers to the dawn prayer, whose long, audible recitation distinguishes it from the afternoon prayer and encourages people despite sleep.
rows.anchor: عبر عنها بالقرآن لأنه مع كونه أعظم أركان الصلاة يطول فيها القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may also be parsed as an accusative exhortation to perform the dawn recitation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نصب على الإغراءن وكأنه عبر عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn recitation is witnessed by the night and day angel groups and delights hearing, heart, and spirit.
rows.anchor: يشهده فريقا الملائكة , وهو أهل لأن يشهده كل أحد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that congregational prayer exceeds solitary prayer by twenty-five degrees and that night and day angels meet at dawn; he cites this verse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : فضل صلاة الجميع على صلاة الواحد خمس وعشرون درجة , وتجتمع ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators infer from the report that prayer is due at the beginning of its time and that praying dawn in the darkness before daybreak is preferable.
rows.anchor: قالوا : وهذا دليل على وجوب الصلاة بأول الوقت , وأن التغليس بصلاة الفجر أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tahajjud means leaving sleep for prayer, with its pronoun referring broadly to the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: أي اترك الهجود - وهو النوم - بالصلاة { به } أي بمطلق القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night prayer is a special added obligation for the Prophet and voluntary extra worship for the community.
rows.anchor: زيادة للنبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم في الفرض وللأمة في التطوع

rows.speaker: عبد الغافر الفارسي
rows.claim: Abd al-Ghafir al-Farisi says nafilah originally means an addition, as in extra gains granted to this community.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الغافر الفارسي في مجمع الغرائب : وأصل النفل الزيادة , ومنه الأنفال الزائدة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله القزاز
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah al-Qazzaz glosses nawafil as gifts or supererogatory benefits, as in calling someone generous in his gifts.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله القزاز : النوافل : الفواضل , ومن هذا يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The late night is associated with answered supplication and closeness to God.
rows.anchor: لأنه الوقت الذي كني فيه عن استجابة الدعاء بالنزول إلى السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Descriptions of divine descent and nearness are metaphors for their consequence, by analogy with rulers opening doors and lowering veils to grant requests.
rows.anchor: وكل ما يعبر به عن الله تعالى مما ينزه سبحانه عن ظاهره يكون كناية عن لازمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uthman ibn Abi al-As’s report continues: at an hour of the night the gates of heaven open and a caller invites supplication that will be answered.
rows.anchor: إن في الليل ساهة يفتح فيها أبواب السماء فينادي مناد : هل من داع فيستجاب له ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ʿasā conveys certainty: God would not promise something and then deprive the recipient; its indirect form also suits royal grandeur.
rows.anchor: وهي هنا لليقين , قالوا : إن عسى تفيد الإطماع , ومن أطمع أحدا في شيء ثم حرمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this station may refer specifically to intercession or more generally to any station the Prophet is enabled to occupy.
rows.anchor: هذا المقام صالحا للشفاعة ولكل مقام يقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that every community follows its prophet on Resurrection Day and asks for intercession until it reaches Muhammad; this is the praiseworthy station.
rows.anchor: وللبخاري في التفسير عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال : إن الناس يصيرون يوم القيامة جثى

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet’s instruction to ask after the call to prayer for Muhammad to receive the praiseworthy station, earning the speaker his intercession.
rows.anchor: وله في التفسير وغيره عن جابر بن عبدالله رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم قال : ( من قال حين يسمع النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith identifies the praiseworthy station especially with the Prophet’s particular intercession; general intercession is available to all without condition.
rows.anchor: يعني - والله أعلم - الشفاعة الخاصة , وأما العامة فللكل بغير شرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks for every worldly and spiritual entry and exit to be sincere and true, since duplicity prevents honor with God.
rows.anchor: يستحق الداخل فيه أن يقال له : أنت صادق في قولك وفعلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because truthfulness alone may not bring victory, the prayer asks for divine proof and power to support the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الصدق في الأمور قد لا يقارنه الظفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for a supporting proof and might hints at the Hijra and its later outcome.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشعار بالهجرة وأنها تكون على الوجه الذي كشف عنه الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth is everything God commanded and revealed to the Prophet; falsehood is everything opposed to it, and its disappearance is decreed from eternity.
rows.anchor: { جاء الحق } وهو كل ما أمرني به ربي وأنزله إلي { وزهق } أي اضمحل وبلط وهلك { الباطل } وهو كل ما خالفه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet entered the Kaaba among 360 idols, struck them with a stick, and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: دخل النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم وحول البيت ستون وثلاثمائة نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the verse to “Truth has come, and falsehood neither begins nor repeats,” from Sabaʾ.
rows.anchor: جاء الحق وما يبدئ الباطل وما يعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is healing for hearts and bodies and mercy for believers, lighting hearts against ignorance and guarding sincere seekers from affliction.
rows.anchor: للقلوب والأبدان { ورحمة } أي إكرام وقوة { للمؤمنين } أي الراسخين في الإيمان

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi calls the Qur’an the solace of lovers and seekers, a clear light that unveils hidden truths and dangers.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : وهو أنس المحبين , وسلوة المشتاقين , وإنه النور المبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejecting the Qur’an after proof increases the wrongdoers’ unbelief and loss, while accepting and reflecting on it increases believers’ faith.
rows.anchor: فكان إعراضهم ذلك زيادة في كفرانهم , كما أن قبول المؤمنين له وإقبالهم على تدبره زيادة في إيمانهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says nobody sits with the Qur’an and leaves without increase or decrease, then recites this verse.
rows.anchor: وفي الدارمي عن قتادة قال : ما جالس القرآن أحد فقام عنه بزيادة أو نقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When blessed, the generic human turns away proudly from the giver.
rows.anchor: أي عن ذكر المنعم كإعراض هؤلاء عند مجيء هذه النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human turns away in pride and blindness, then despairs when touched by harm, except those God preserves from the devil’s power.
rows.anchor: أي تباعد تكبرا { بجانبه } بطرا وعمى عن الحقائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When harmed, the generic human becomes deeply hopeless and distrustful of God’s mercy, except those He preserves.
rows.anchor: أي شديد اليأس هلعا وقلة ثقة بما عنده من رحمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent generalization about human ingratitude is restricted to the prodigal in 10:12 and balanced by the patient in 11:11; the author says these exceptions are few.
rows.anchor: بأن هذا في المسرفين دون غيرهم , وبقوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person acts according to a way shaped by the soul’s character and God-given disposition; only God fully knows who is best guided.
rows.anchor: طريقته التي تشاكل روحه وتشاكل ما طبعنا عليه من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grateful and patient act rightly in piety and excellence and receive reward, while the more astray receive punishment; God knows their created traits directly.
rows.anchor: فيشكر ويصبر احتسابا فيعطيه الثواب , ومن هو أضل سبيلا , فيحل به العقاب

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Ahmad transmits from Abu al-Darda through a disconnected chain a saying that a moved mountain is believable but a person changing his ingrained character is not.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم قال : ( إذا سمعتم بجبل زال عن مكانه فصدقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about the spirit is posed as a test and asks what it is, whether bodily or not, whether caused by bodily mixtures, and whether eternal or created.
rows.anchor: ماهي ؟ هل هي جسم أم لا ؟ وهل هي متولدة من امتزاج الطبائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit belongs to God’s direct command: creation through stages is called khalq, while bringing something from nonbeing without mediation is called amr; the spirit is created but not developed through causes.
rows.anchor: إن الخلق قسمان : ما كان بتسبيب وتنمية وتطوير

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: The preferred Sunni view is that the spirit is a subtle created body flowing through the body like rosewater through a rose.
rows.anchor: وهي جسم لطيف سار في البدن كماء الورد في الورد على الصحيح عند أهل السنة

rows.speaker: السلف
rows.claim: The early generations refrained from probing the spirit out of proper etiquette, seeing silence as more appropriate than further speculation.
rows.anchor: وأمسك السلف عن الإمعان في الكلام على الروح أدبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioners neglect the useful spiritual Qur’an for an obscure physical spirit, whose many questions admit no proof; ignorance of a thing’s precise nature does not mean it does not exist.
rows.anchor: ولا يلزم من عدم العلم بحقيقته المخصوصة نفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing spirit’s progress from ignorance to knowledge proves it is created; human knowledge is little relative to God’s, including among scriptural scholars.
rows.anchor: فإنه يكون في المبدإ جاهلا ثم يحدث له العلم شيئا بعد شيء , وكل متغير حادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question wastes effort on a difficult matter with no benefit while ignoring clear religious and worldly guidance whose neglect causes ruin.
rows.anchor: أن تسألوا عما لا يضركم الجهل به , ويتوقف إثباته على أمور دقيقة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In an authentic report, Ibn Masud says Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit while he walked with him in Medina; revelation came and he recited this verse.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه كان يمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم في المدينة , فسأله اليهود عن الروح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that before the Hijra Quraysh asked Jews how to test the Prophet; they suggested questions about the spirit, the Companions of the Cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn.
rows.anchor: أن قريشا أرسلت إلى اليهود قبل الهجرة تسألهم عن النبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In this report the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying “if God wills”; revelation was delayed fifteen nights, with other reports saying forty or twelve, causing him grief amid Meccan rumors.
rows.anchor: فمكث فيما يذكرون خمس عشرة ليلة , لا يحدث الله إليه في ذلك وحيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report in Musnad Abi Yaʿla likewise says Quraysh asked Jews for a test and then asked the Prophet about the spirit.
rows.anchor: وفي مسند أبي يعلى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : قالت قريش ليهود : أعطونا شيئا نسأل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparently conflicting accounts are reconciled by taking the first as the occasion of revelation and later questioning as a repeated revelation confirming the same sufficient answer.
rows.anchor: فإنه محمول على أنه نزل للسبب الأول , فلما سئل عنه النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم ثانيا لم يجب فيه بالجواب الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delayed answer proves the Qur’an is from God: the Prophet could not compose a reply himself despite the serious damage the delay did to his reputation.
rows.anchor: وفي تأخير الجواب في هذا الأمر برهان قاطع لقريش وكل من له أدنى لب على صدق النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم في أن هذا القرآن من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit belongs to the hidden realm of command, so its question is placed in al-Isra, linked to the hidden mystery of the ascent, and separated from worldly questions about the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فصلت عن السؤالين الآخرين , لأنهما من عالم الملك , وسيأتي بقية الكلام على هذا في سورة الكهف

none: The segment contains only the Qur’an text and heading, with no commentary to record.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing attempts to alter revelation and expel the Messenger, the verse warns that God could remove the Qur’an and leave people with their little knowledge and ignorance.
rows.anchor: تنبيها لهم على أنه لو شاء لذهب بسبب هذا العلم القليل الذي وهبهموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No protector could bring the revelation back against God; the emphatic oath construction answers the conditional by asserting certain removal if God willed.
rows.anchor: ولامه موطئة للقسم , وأجاب عن القسم بما أغنى عن جواب الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing emphasizes the revelation’s subject; the author says God alone can restore or replace it by mercy.
rows.anchor: أي لكن تجد { رحمة } مبتدئة وكائنة { من ربك } أي المحسن إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continued gift of revelation is an immense favor to the Prophet and his community, so the verse strongly emphasizes its greatness.
rows.anchor: ولما كان في إنزاله إليه ثم إبقائه لديه من النعمة عليه وعلى أمته ما لا يحصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Qur’an will disappear at the end of time from both written copies and people’s hearts; the author says this verse implies that possibility.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد أنه يذهب بالقرآن في آخر الزمان , يسري بما في المصاحف وبما في القلوبن وقد أفهمت ذلك هذه الآية
